correctness.rationale: Complete Eratosthenes and square-divisor sieves cover all integers in the stated finite range, selecting 879429 primes in the progression. Both independent implementations give precisely 21 four-offset failures, only the last failing the fifth allowable offset, and the last has a squarefree sixth remainder. Explicit square divisors and the modulus-nine obstruction close every prior exponent. The proof addresses the whole claimed finite domain.

The exact threshold and full minimality are not implied by the prior asymptotic density or broad odd-integer existence results.
